title: Exact restriction comparison detected by finite cochain models
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A',\mathcal B,\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with enough injectives in $\mathcal A,\mathcal A'$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G':\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$ be additive left exact functors with ordinary total right derived functors [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] computed on nonnegative injective resolutions. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Ch}^{[0,r]}(\mathcal B)$ and $F':\mathcal A'\to\operatorname{Ch}^{[0,r]}(\mathcal B')$ have exact degree functors, for a fixed $r\geq0$, and natural augmentations $e:G(-)[0]\to F$ and $e':G'(-)[0]\to F'$ that are quasi-isomorphisms on injective objects. Use the normalized natural derived isomorphisms $\lambda:QF\xrightarrow{\sim}RG(-[0])$ and $\lambda':QF'\xrightarrow{\sim}RG'(-[0])$ specified in [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model]. Let $U:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$, $V:\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ be exact additive functors and suppose natural isomorphisms $\gamma:GU\xrightarrow{\sim}VG'$ and $\theta:FU\xrightarrow{\sim}VF'$ are given, with $\theta\circ e_U=(Ve')\circ\gamma[0]$. Write $D(V)$ for the induced functor on ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For $X'\in\mathcal A'$, choose nonnegative injective resolutions $t:X'[0]\to J^\bullet$ and $s:UX'[0]\to I^\bullet$. There is a chain map $\beta:UJ^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ with $\beta\circ Ut=s$. Every such $\beta$ has $G(\beta)$ a quasi-isomorphism; any two are homotopic and define the same derived morphism after applying $G$. With normalized comparisons $\rho_s:RG(UX'[0])\cong QG(I^\bullet)$ and $\rho'_t:RG'(X'[0])\cong QG'(J^\bullet)$, set
$$\alpha_{X'}=D(V)(\rho'_t)^{-1}\circ Q(\gamma_{J^\bullet})\circ QG(\beta)^{-1}\circ\rho_s:RG(UX'[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}D(V)RG'(X'[0]).$$
This is independent of resolutions and extensions, is natural in $X'$, and satisfies
$$\alpha_{X'}\circ\lambda_{UX'}=D(V)(\lambda'_{X'})\circ Q(\theta_{X'}).$$
Its inverse is the comparison obtained by applying the unit of $RG$ to $UJ^\bullet$ and using the augmentation $Ut$ and $\gamma$; in particular it is normalized by that unit. The conclusion imposes no preservation of injectives by $U$.

proof.text: Exactness of $U$ and the natural cohomology identification in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] make $Ut:UX'[0]\to UJ^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism. It is degreewise monic: $t^0$ identifies $X'$ with $\ker(d_J^0)$ because $J$ is nonnegative; all other source terms are zero, and exact $U$ preserves kernels. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] to $Ut$ and $s$, with target the nonnegative complex of injectives $I$, to obtain $\beta$ with $\beta Ut=s$. For two extensions apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] to $Ut$, since their restrictions are equal. If $h$ is the resulting homotopy, additivity gives $G(\beta_1)-G(\beta_2)=d_{GI}G(h)+G(h)d_{GUJ}$. Thus $G(h)$ is a homotopy, and the two maps have equal images under the localization of the homotopy category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift), part (2), and 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy); exact-functor cohomology applied to U

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model] separately to $(G,F,e,s)$ and $(G',F',e',t)$. Write $T_s=\operatorname{Tot}(F^a(I^b))$ and $T'_t=\operatorname{Tot}(F'^a(J^b))$, using [def-sp-double-complex-total] with differential $d_F+(-1)^a d_I$. The maps $c_s:F(UX')\to T_s$, $b_s:G(I)\to T_s$, $c'_t:F'(X')\to T'_t$ and $b'_t:G'(J)\to T'_t$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Moreover $\lambda_{UX'}=\rho_s^{-1}Q(b_s)^{-1}Q(c_s)$ and $\lambda'_{X'}=(\rho'_t)^{-1}Q(b'_t)^{-1}Q(c'_t)$. All hypotheses hold separately in the two abelian categories: the degree functors are exact, both resolutions consist of injectives, and the respective augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms on these terms.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), as packaged in the normalized finite-exact-complex model

proof.text:
Form $B^{a,b}=F^a(UJ^b)$ and $T_U=\operatorname{Tot}B$ with the same signs. Its degree-$n$ sum has only $0\leq a\leq\min(r,n)$, so it exists using finite biproducts. The component maps $\theta_{J^b}^a$ induce a chain isomorphism $\Theta:T_U\xrightarrow{\sim}V(T'_t)$: use the canonical finite-biproduct comparison for additive $V$. Explicitly this comparison and its inverse are determined by the biproduct inclusions and projections; their composites are identities by the biproduct equations. Naturality of $\theta$ in $d_J$ and its chain-map property in $a$ show that both total differential blocks commute, including $(-1)^a$. Define $c:F(UX')\to T_U$ from $F(Ut)$ along $b=0$, and $b:G(UJ)\to T_U$ from $e_{UJ^b}$ along $a=0$. The chain-map property of $Ut$ and naturality of $e$ make these chain maps. On the axes the assumed augmentation compatibility and naturality of $\theta$ give respectively
$$\Theta b=V(b'_t)\gamma_J,\qquad \Theta c=V(c'_t)\theta_{X'}.$$
These equalities hold on each diagonal summand; the axis signs are $1$.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), explicit augmentation maps and second-variable variant; componentwise finite-biproduct calculation

proof.text: For each $b\geq0$, the equality $\theta_{J^b}e_{UJ^b}=V(e'_{J^b})\gamma_{J^b}[0]$ shows that $e_{UJ^b}$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Indeed $J^b$ is injective, so $e'_{J^b}$ is one by hypothesis, and exact $V$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. For $b<0$ all terms are zero. Apply [lem-sc-finite-strip-row-augmentation] to $B$, with its strip parameter $r+1$ and with the row maps $e_{UJ^b}$ and total augmentation $b$. Its support requirement is exactly $0\leq a<r+1$; all totals exist by the finite diagonal sums above. Hence $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism even though the $UJ^b$ need not be injective. Also $V(c'_t)$ is a quasi-isomorphism by exactness of $V$, since [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model] supplies that property for $c'_t$. The equation $\Theta c=V(c'_t)\theta_{X'}$ now proves that $c$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let $k=\operatorname{Tot}(F(\beta)):T_U\to T_s$, with component $F^a(\beta^b)$ on each summand. Naturality of $e$ gives $kb=b_sG(\beta)$, and $\beta Ut=s$ gives $kc=c_s$, both as literal chain-map equalities on their supporting axes. Since $c,c_s$ are quasi-isomorphisms, applying each $H^n$ to the latter equality shows that $H^n(k)$ is invertible. Since $k,b,b_s$ are quasi-isomorphisms, applying each $H^n$ to the former equality shows that $H^n(G(\beta))$ is invertible. This proves the assertion for every extension $\beta$. Consequently all inverses in the stated formula for $\alpha_{X'}$ exist after $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and that formula defines an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), augmentation naturality and two-of-three on cohomology

proof.text:
In this step suppress $Q$ on chain maps, write $V$ for $D(V)$, and use right-to-left composition. From $kb=b_sG\beta$ and $kc=c_s$ we have $(G\beta)^{-1}b_s^{-1}c_s=b^{-1}c$. From $\Theta b=V(b'_t)\gamma_J$ and $\Theta c=V(c'_t)\theta_{X'}$ we have $\gamma_Jb^{-1}c=V(b'_t)^{-1}V(c'_t)\theta_{X'}$. Substitute these two equalities and the two formulas for $\lambda$ from [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model] into the definition of $\alpha$:
$$\alpha_{X'}\lambda_{UX'}=V(\rho'_t)^{-1}\gamma_J(G\beta)^{-1}b_s^{-1}c_s
=V(\rho'_t)^{-1}V(b'_t)^{-1}V(c'_t)\theta_{X'}
=V(\lambda'_{X'})\theta_{X'}.$$
Thus the required equation holds for the specific resolution-and-extension formula in the statement.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient comparison: explicit cancellation of the finite-model augmentation squares

proof.text:
Since $\lambda_{UX'}$ is invertible, the equation just proved determines
$$\alpha_{X'}=D(V)(\lambda'_{X'})\,Q(\theta_{X'})\,\lambda_{UX'}^{-1}.$$
The two $\lambda$'s are independent of resolutions and natural by [lem-sfb-finite-exact-complex-derived-model], and $\theta$ is a given natural isomorphism. This expression therefore proves independence from both resolutions and from $\beta$. For $f:X'\to Y'$, substitute the naturality equations for $\lambda$, $\lambda'$ and $\theta$ into this expression to obtain $D(V)RG'(f[0])\alpha_{X'}=\alpha_{Y'}RG(Uf[0])$, proving naturality in $X'$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient comparison: independence and naturality from the normalized model formula

proof.text:
Finally retain $Q$ explicitly and let $\eta$ be the unit of $RG$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The stipulated unit normalization is $\rho_s=\eta_I^{-1}RG(Qs)$. Naturality of $\eta$ on $\beta$ gives $\eta_IQG(\beta)=RG(Q\beta)\eta_{UJ}$. Since $s=\beta Ut$ and $Q(Ut),Q\beta$ are invertible (the latter because both $Ut$ and $s$ are quasi-isomorphisms), cancellation yields
$$\rho_s^{-1}QG(\beta)=RG(Q(Ut))^{-1}\eta_{UJ}.$$
Taking the inverse of the displayed definition of $\alpha$ consequently gives
$$\alpha_{X'}^{-1}=RG(Q(Ut))^{-1}\eta_{UJ}\,Q(\gamma_J)^{-1}D(V)(\rho'_t).$$
This is exactly the comparison that first represents $RG'(X'[0])$ by $QG'(J)$, identifies $VG'(J)$ with $G(UJ)$ by $\gamma^{-1}$, applies the unit at $UJ$, and inverts the augmentation $Ut$ under $RG$. It proves the claimed unit normalization without using injectivity of any $UJ^b$.
